action: Renew any authentication secret that is or may be compromised, enforce strong authentication and tight control of privileged accounts, filter access to block bulk extraction, and test internet-facing applications for IDOR flaws.
exec: The French state's own post-mortem shows stolen credentials, weak sign-in and simple web flaws, not novel exploits, driving public-sector data loss.
plain: France's cyber agency says 64 new data breaches reached it since September 30, five at ministries or their agencies. Known causes: stolen passwords, accounts without a second sign-in step, or web pages that exposed other people's files.

key_findings: 64 new data violations were reported since the September 30 report; five concern ministries or subordinate bodies and are handled with ANSSI support.
New cases: about 1.2 million CAF/VACAF case files, over 60,000 France Travail agents and professionals, 30,500 ASP DEFI users, over 1,000 OFB permit users, about 100 foreign ministry library users.
25 of 30 education academies had incidents between July and September 2026; intruders reused valid credentials and moved across the interministerial state network.
Every breach used weaknesses already seen: missing or weak MFA, infostealer-compromised accounts, subcontractor exposure, IDOR flaws and configuration defects.
At France Travail a compromised agent account, with second-factor (SMS) validation, allowed exfiltration; elsewhere MFA stopped logins with stolen VPN certificates.
recommendations: Immediately renew authentication secrets that are compromised or suspected to be.
Enforce strong authentication everywhere and strictly control privileged accounts.
Harden access filtering to prevent data exfiltration.
Strengthen security of internet-exposed applications and those linked to third-party networks.
Notify affected people where the nature of the data requires it.

summary: CERT-FR's second REACTIV situation report counts 64 new data violations since September 30, five of them at ministries or their agencies: a foreign ministry library portal, the OFB permit portal, France Travail (over 60,000 agents and professionals), CAF's VACAF (about 1.2 million case files) and the ASP DEFI portal (30,500 users). ANSSI found no new weakness types: missing multi-factor sign-in, infostealer-stolen accounts, supplier exposure and IDOR flaws recur.
title: ANSSI's second REACTIV report details October data leaks across French state bodies
